title: Replacement Appraisal Charge on Short-Sale Statements — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction
content:
## Short-sale statement replacement appraisal charge — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction

On the payoff case of an Approved Short Sale Payoff requested by the borrower of record, the short-sale statement replacement appraisal charge enters the short-sale statement balance. It is read from the loan's maturity case under the Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases product: its appraisal date, its due-and-payable date, the entries recording granted extensions, and the appraisal ordering period of the case's plan.

**Rule.** The short-sale statement replacement appraisal charge is USD 295.00, the update appraisal fee, when the maturity case's appraisal date falls on or after the effective date of the case's latest granted extension and no more than the case plan's appraisal ordering period of calendar days after it; it is USD 395.00, the replacement appraisal fee, when that does not hold and the appraisal date is more than the appraisal ordering period of calendar days after the case's due-and-payable date; a case with no appraisal date, or whose appraisal falls within neither span, carries nothing (0.00).

**Order of the tests.** The first span (on or after the latest granted extension, within the ordering period) is tested first; only where it does not hold is the second span tested. A case with no granted extension can meet only the second span.

### Cases

| Hypothetical maturity case (ordering period taken as 30 days for the illustration) | Result |
|---|---|
| Latest granted extension effective on day 0; appraisal dated day 0 | update fee, USD 295.00 |
| Latest granted extension effective on day 0; appraisal dated day 30 | update fee, USD 295.00 |
| Latest granted extension effective on day 0; appraisal dated day 31; due-and-payable date 200 days before the appraisal | replacement fee, USD 395.00 |
| No granted extension; appraisal dated 45 days after the due-and-payable date | replacement fee, USD 395.00 |
| No granted extension; appraisal dated 20 days after the due-and-payable date | nothing |
| No appraisal date on the case | nothing |

The ordering period of 30 days in the table is a hypothetical value; the period that applies is the one set by the maturity case's plan.
